```text
68	**Manifest creation** ([build_project.py](scripts/build_project.py) + [auto_select.py](scripts/auto_select.py)):

70	regex+brace-matcher → keeps a method iff it exists in **both** trees with the **same name+arity** but
71	a **changed normalized body** → keeps only **auto-fuzzable** ones (every param is scalar / String /
72	primitive array) → writes `manifest.json` + renamed `<Class>{Original,Refactored}.java` snapshots
73	into the **same package** (so both compile into one JVM).
74	
75	**Manifest `params` + `static` are read from the REFACTORED signature**
76	([build_project.py:87](scripts/build_project.py#L87), `classify(n[key]...)` where `n` = refactored).
77	Name+arity are shared by construction (pairing key = `name/paramCount`). Verified: **0 signature
78	disagreements** across all 62 apex-core methods, so original-vs-refactored is moot in practice.
79	**Conclusion: correct approach for signature-preserving refactorings.** If a refactoring *changes* a
80	param type → runtime `NoSuchMethodException` → **ERROR** (fail-safe); if it changes arity → the
81	methods don't pair → silently **dropped** (a known blind spot, never a false EQUIVALENT).
82	
83	**The fuzz loop** ([GenericDifferential.java](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java)):
84	Jazzer (libFuzzer-based, coverage-guided) drives a thin per-method harness →
85	`GenericDifferential.run(data, project, id)` → looks the spec up in the manifest → resolves **both**
86	`Original` and `Refactored` classes → builds the receiver (recursive ctor synthesis for instance
87	methods) and args **once** from the `FuzzedDataProvider` using the manifest `params` as the decode
88	schema → `copy()`s them per side → invokes each on a **3 s watchdog thread** → oracle compares. Jazzer
89	generates raw **byte inputs at runtime** (not test files); the only per-method *file* is the harness,
90	written by [gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) (Python). Corpus of "interesting" byte inputs
91	persists under `target/fuzz-cwd/.cifuzz-corpus/`.
92	
93	**The oracle** (`equivalent()`): DIVERGENT iff exception **types** differ, or (neither threw)
94	scalar/JDK **return values** differ. One-sided **TIMEOUT is inconclusive** (not divergent). Return
95	type used for comparability comes from the **original** method (`oM.getReturnType()`) — mirror image
96	of the params-from-refactored rule.

121	
122	| Dimension | Paper (Eq@DFuzz) | Our tool |
123	|---|---|---|
124	| Language | Python | Java |
125	| Fuzzer | Atheris (libFuzzer) | Jazzer (libFuzzer) — sibling |
126	| Unit tested | whole function / program | individual **changed method** (source-diffed) |
127	| Input typing | GPT-4-inferred + manually-validated constraints | heuristic scalar-only from signature |
128	| Complex-object args | handled via constraints | **excluded** at manifest time |
129	| Oracle | output equality only | return value **+ exception type**; TIMEOUT = inconclusive |
130	| Receiver/ctors | N/A (functional Python) | recursive ctor synthesis |
131	| Budget | fixed input count (2000 fn / 1000 prog) | wall-clock (1 min/method) |
132	| Deliverable | empirical metric + study | reusable per-method report + JaCoCo coverage |
133	
134	Paper's headline results: LLMs produce **19–35% non-equivalent** refactorings; **~21%** of those pass
135	the datasets' existing test suites (i.e., tests overestimate equivalence).

137	## The pipeline (reference)
138	
139	One entry point chains four scripts ([run.py](run.py)):
140	
141	| Step | Script | Produces |
142	|------|--------|----------|
143	| 1 | [build_project.py](scripts/build_project.py) `<p> --original <o> --refactored <r>` | `manifest.json` + `<Class>{Original,Refactored}` snapshots |
144	| 2 | [prune.py](scripts/prune.py) `<p>` | iterative `mvn -P<p> test-compile`; drops pairs that won't compile (also rewrites the manifest) |
145	| 3 | [gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) `<p> <dur>` | one Jazzer harness per manifest method |
146	| 4 | [run_project.py](scripts/run_project.py) `<p>` | fuzz + JaCoCo coverage → `reports/<p>/auto-fuzz-report.md` |
147	
148	`src/test/Dataset/`, `src/test/fuzzing/`, `src/test/resources/`, `reports/`, `target/` are all
149	**generated + git-ignored** — regenerate with `run.py`. (They exist on disk here from real runs.)
150	
151	## Key files
152	
153	- [src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java)
154	  — the shared reflection engine + oracle. Project-agnostic.
155	- [scripts/build_project.py](scripts/build_project.py) — the two-tree diff → manifest + snapshots.
156	  Params/`static` read from the **refactored** signature (line 87).
157	- [scripts/auto_select.py](scripts/auto_select.py) — heuristic Java-signature parsing + `classify()`
158	  (AUTO_FUZZABLE = scalar/String/primitive-array args only).
159	- [pom.xml](pom.xml) — engine-only base + one `<profile id="apex-core">`. Add a sibling profile per
160	  new project.
161	
162	## Gotchas / limitations
163	
164	- **Fuzzing is sound for non-equivalence, incomplete for equivalence.** A DIVERGENT is a real witness;
165	  **EQUIVALENT only means "no divergence found in the budget," never a proof.** Trust it in proportion
166	  to the **Branch** column (`4/4` trustworthy; `0/0` branchless — read Line).
167	- **Coverage rewards new edges, not new disagreements** — value-only divergences with identical
168	  control flow get no search guidance (found only by luck).
169	- **Literal-only changes are invisible:** `strip_noise()` blanks string/char literal *contents*, so
170	  `return "alpha"` vs `return "beta"` normalizes identically and never enters the manifest. Verified.
171	- **Oracle is shallow:** exception *type* only (not messages), no side-effect / mutated-receiver
172	  comparison, non-comparable return types collapse to a null-ness check.
173	- **One finding halts the run** (AssertionError → Jazzer stops) — DIVERGENT logs are ~5 s, EQUIVALENT
174	  ~67 s. You get one divergence per method per run, not an enumeration.
175	- **Corpus lives under `target/`** → `mvn clean` or a fresh checkout wipes it; every method restarts
176	  from zero coverage. Move it outside `target/` to let coverage compound across sessions.
177	- **Rename artifacts:** `toString`/`hashCode` can show DIVERGENT purely because the class is renamed to
178	  `…Original`/`…Refactored`. Discard those.
179	- **Signature-changing refactorings** are out of scope (ERROR or dropped, per above).
180
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Differential "first tester" — one entry point: two source trees in, one report out.
4	
5	    python3 run.py <project> --original <origTree> --refactored <refTree> [options]
6	
7	It chains the four pipeline steps (each is a standalone script under scripts/):
8	
9	    1. build_project.py   diff original vs refactored -> manifest.json + <Class>{Original,Refactored} snapshots
10	    2. prune.py           iterative `./mvnw test-compile`; drop pairs whose deps don't resolve
11	    3. gen_harnesses.py   one thin Jazzer harness per manifest method
12	    4. run_project.py     fuzz each method + JaCoCo coverage -> reports/<project>/auto-fuzz-report.md
13	
14	Requires Maven + a JDK for steps 2-4 (the fuzzing itself). Step 1 is pure Python.
15	The target project's own dependencies must be resolvable (for apex-core: run
16	scripts/setup_deps.sh first, or add them to the -P<project> profile in pom.xml).
17	
18	Example (apex-core, from the bundled example trees):
19	    scripts/setup_deps.sh /path/to/built/apex-core
20	    python3 run.py apex-core --original examples/apex-core/original \\
21	                             --refactored examples/apex-core/refactored
22	"""
23	import argparse
24	import os
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	
28	MODULE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
29	SCRIPTS = os.path.join(MODULE, "scripts")
30	
31	
32	def step(title, argv):
33	    print(f"\n=== {title} ===\n  $ {' '.join(argv)}", flush=True)
34	    r = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=MODULE)
35	    if r.returncode != 0:
36	        print(f"\nFAILED at: {title} (exit {r.returncode})", file=sys.stderr)
37	        sys.exit(r.returncode)
38	
39	
40	def py(script, *args):
41	    return [sys.executable, os.path.join(SCRIPTS, script), *args]
42	
43	
44	def main():
45	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
46	    ap.add_argument("project", help="profile id in pom.xml (e.g. apex-core)")
47	    ap.add_argument("--original", required=True, help="original source tree root")
48	    ap.add_argument("--refactored", required=True, help="refactored source tree root")
49	    ap.add_argument("--duration", default="1m", help="Jazzer maxDuration per method (default 1m)")
50	    ap.add_argument("--max", type=int, default=0, help="only run the first N methods (smoke test)")
51	    ap.add_argument("--skip-build", action="store_true", help="reuse existing manifest/snapshots")
52	    ap.add_argument("--skip-prune", action="store_true", help="skip the compile-and-drop gate")
53	    args = ap.parse_args()
54	
55	    if not args.skip_build:
56	        step("1/4 build manifest + snapshots",
57	             py("build_project.py", args.project, "--original", args.original, "--refactored", args.refactored))
58	    if not args.skip_prune:
59	        step("2/4 prune uncompilable pairs", py("prune.py", args.project))
60	    step("3/4 generate harnesses", py("gen_harnesses.py", args.project, args.duration))
61	    run_argv = py("run_project.py", args.project)
62	    if args.max:
63	        run_argv += ["--max", str(args.max)]
64	    step("4/4 fuzz + coverage -> report", run_argv)
65	
66	    report = os.path.join(MODULE, "reports", args.project, "auto-fuzz-report.md")
67	    print(f"\nDONE. Report: {report}")
68	
69	
70	if __name__ == "__main__":
71	    main()
72
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Generate one thin Jazzer harness per method from a project's manifest.json.
4	
5	Each harness is namespaced in package fuzz.auto.<projkey> (so corpora/reports stay
6	per-project) and just calls GenericDifferential.run(data, project, id) — the spec lives in
7	the manifest, not in the harness.
8	
9	Usage: gen_harnesses.py <project> [maxDuration=1m]
10	"""
11	import json
12	import os
13	import sys
14	
15	MODULE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
16	
17	TEMPLATE = '''package fuzz.auto.{projkey};
18	
19	import com.code_intelligence.jazzer.api.FuzzedDataProvider;
20	import com.code_intelligence.jazzer.junit.FuzzTest;
21	
22	import fuzz.auto.GenericDifferential;
23	
24	/** AUTO-GENERATED from src/test/resources/{project}/manifest.json — fuzzes {id}. */
25	public class {harness}
26	{{
27	  @FuzzTest(maxDuration = "{dur}")
28	  public void differential(FuzzedDataProvider data) throws Throwable
29	  {{
30	    GenericDifferential.run(data, "{project}", "{id}");
31	  }}
32	}}
33	'''
34	
35	
36	def main(project, dur):
37	    projkey = project.replace("-", "_")
38	    man = json.load(open(os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/resources", project, "manifest.json")))
39	    # harnesses live in a SEPARATE tree from the project source (Dataset/), per-project
40	    outdir = os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/fuzzing", project, "fuzz/auto", projkey)
41	    if os.path.isdir(outdir):
42	        for f in os.listdir(outdir):
43	            if f.endswith("FuzzTest.java"):
44	                os.remove(os.path.join(outdir, f))
45	    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
46	    for e in man["methods"]:
47	        harness = "Auto_" + e["id"].replace(".", "_") + "_FuzzTest"
48	        open(os.path.join(outdir, harness + ".java"), "w").write(
49	            TEMPLATE.format(projkey=projkey, project=project, id=e["id"], harness=harness, dur=dur))
50	    print(f"generated {len(man['methods'])} harnesses in fuzz.auto.{projkey} (maxDuration={dur})")
51	
52	
53	if __name__ == "__main__":
54	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
55	        print(__doc__)
56	        sys.exit(2)
57	    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "1m")
58
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Run the differential-fuzzing suite for one project, driven by its manifest.json.
4	
5	For each method: JAZZER_FUZZ=1 ./mvnw test on its generated harness (1 min via maxDuration),
6	classify EQUIVALENT / DIVERGENT / ERROR, measure per-method JaCoCo branch/line coverage,
7	and write reports/<project>/auto-fuzz-report.md (same columns as before).
8	
9	A one-sided watchdog TIMEOUT is treated as inconclusive by the engine (not divergent).
10	
11	Usage: run_project.py <project> [--max N] [--regression]
12	"""
13	import glob 
14	import json
15	import os
16	import re
17	import subprocess
18	import sys
19	import time
20	
21	MODULE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
22	
23	
24	def cov_classpath():
25	    core = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.m2/repository/org/jacoco/org.jacoco.core/0.8.11/org.jacoco.core-0.8.11.jar"))
26	    asm = os.path.expanduser("~/.m2/repository/org/ow2/asm")
27	    jars = [f"{MODULE}/target/covtool"]
28	    if core:
29	        jars.append(core[0])
30	    for a in ("asm/9.6/asm-9.6.jar", "asm-commons/9.6/asm-commons-9.6.jar",
31	              "asm-tree/9.6/asm-tree-9.6.jar", "asm-analysis/9.6/asm-analysis-9.6.jar"):
32	        jars.append(os.path.join(asm, a))
33	    return ":".join(jars)
34	
35	
36	def harness_duration(project):
37	    """Read the maxDuration the harnesses were generated with (for the report header)."""
38	    projkey = project.replace("-", "_")
39	    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/fuzzing", project, "fuzz/auto", projkey, "*FuzzTest.java"))
40	    if files:
41	        mm = re.search(r'maxDuration\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', open(files[0]).read())
42	        if mm:
43	            return mm.group(1)
44	    return "?"
45	
46	
47	def constructible(entry, project):
48	    """Whether it is worth launching a fuzz run for this entry at all.
49	
50	    Deliberately almost always True. The old version pre-skipped, by source regex, every instance
51	    method on an abstract class or one with no public constructor — which is precisely the set the
52	    engine can now handle, via autofuzz and concrete-subtype substitution. Keeping that filter
53	    would have silently cancelled the whole point of the change.
54	
55	    The only remaining pre-skip is a missing snapshot file, which means the pair was pruned and
56	    there is nothing on the classpath to invoke. Everything else runs, and the engine decides at
57	    runtime, printing [SKIP] with a specific reason when it truly cannot build a receiver.
58	    """
59	    if entry["static"]:
60	        return True
61	    path = os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/Dataset", project,
62	                        entry["refactored"].replace(".", "/") + ".java")
63	    return os.path.isfile(path)
64	
65	
66	def coverage(cp, refsimple, method):
67	    exe = os.path.join(MODULE, "target/jacoco.exec")
68	    if not os.path.exists(exe):
69	        return "n/a", "n/a"
70	    p = subprocess.run(["java", "-cp", cp, "CovReport", exe, f"{MODULE}/target/test-classes", refsimple, method],
71	                       capture_output=True, text=True)
72	    line = p.stdout.strip().splitlines()[0] if p.stdout.strip() else ""
73	    b = re.search(r"branch=(\d+/\d+)", line)
74	    l = re.search(r"line=(\d+/\d+)", line)
75	    return (b.group(1) if b else "n/a"), (l.group(1) if l else "n/a")
76	
77	
78	def main(project, max_n, mode):
79	    projkey = project.replace("-", "_")
80	    man = json.load(open(os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/resources", project, "manifest.json")))
81	    entries = man["methods"][:max_n] if max_n else man["methods"]
82	    dur = harness_duration(project)
83	    cp = cov_classpath()
84	    os.makedirs(f"{MODULE}/target/covtool", exist_ok=True)
85	    subprocess.run(["javac", "-cp", cp.split(":")[1] if ":" in cp else cp, "-d", f"{MODULE}/target/covtool",
86	                    f"{MODULE}/scripts/CovReport.java"], capture_output=True)
87	
88	    logdir = os.path.join(MODULE, "target/fuzz-logs", project)
89	    os.makedirs(logdir, exist_ok=True)
90	    repdir = os.path.join(MODULE, "reports", project)
91	    os.makedirs(repdir, exist_ok=True)
92	    report = os.path.join(repdir, "auto-fuzz-report.md")
93	
94	    env = dict(os.environ)
95	    if mode == "fuzz":
96	        env["JAZZER_FUZZ"] = "1"
97	    else:
98	        env.pop("JAZZER_FUZZ", None)
99	
100	    with open(report, "w") as r:
101	        r.write(f"# Differential-Fuzzing Report — {project} ({man.get('model','qwen')})\n\n")
102	        r.write(f"- Generated: {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}  ·  Mode: **{mode}**  ·  {dur}/method\n")
103	        r.write(f"- {len(entries)} changed methods (manifest-driven; original=<Class>Original, refactored=<Class>Refactored).\n")
104	        r.write("- Branch/Line = JaCoCo per-method coverage. DIVERGENT = exception-type or return-value mismatch (one-sided TIMEOUT is NOT counted).\n\n")
105	        r.write("| Method | Result | Tests (fail) | Branch | Line | Evidence |\n")
106	        r.write("|--------|--------|--------------|--------|------|----------|\n")
107	
108	    eq = div = err = skip = find = never = 0
109	    for i, e in enumerate(entries, 1):
110	        harness = f"fuzz.auto.{projkey}.Auto_" + e["id"].replace(".", "_") + "_FuzzTest"
111	        log = os.path.join(logdir, e["id"].replace(".", "_") + ".log")
112	        refsimple = e["refactored"].split(".")[-1]
113	        print(f"  [{i}/{len(entries)}] {e['id']} ({e.get('kind','?')}) ...", end=" ", flush=True)
114	        if not constructible(e, project):
115	            skip += 1
116	            print("SKIP (snapshot pruned)")
117	            with open(report, "a") as r:
118	                r.write(f"| {e['id']} | **SKIP** | - (-) | n/a | n/a | snapshot pruned, not on classpath |\n")
119	            continue
120	        exe = os.path.join(MODULE, "target/jacoco.exec")
121	        if os.path.exists(exe):
122	            os.remove(exe)
123	        with open(log, "w") as lf:
124	            subprocess.run(["timeout", "240", "./mvnw", f"-P{project}", "test", f"-Dtest={harness}",
125	                            "-Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false", "-Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true"],
126	                           cwd=MODULE, env=env, stdout=lf, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
127	        out = open(log, errors="replace").read()
128	        m = re.search(r"Tests run: (\d+), Failures: (\d+), Errors: (\d+)", out)
129	        runs = m.group(1) if m else "?"
130	        fe = (int(m.group(2)) + int(m.group(3))) if m else 0
131	        branch, line = coverage(cp, refsimple, e["method"])
132	        if "DIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH" in out:
133	            div += 1
134	            om = re.search(r"original  : (.+)", out)
135	            rm = re.search(r"refactored: (.+)", out)
136	            res = "DIVERGENT"
137	            ev = (f"orig: {om.group(1).strip()[:30]} vs ref: {rm.group(1).strip()[:30]}"
138	                  if om and rm else "mismatch (see log)")
139	        elif "[SKIP]" in out:
140	            sm = re.search(r"\[SKIP\].*?— (.+)", out)
141	            res, ev = "SKIP", (sm.group(1).strip()[:60] if sm else "receiver not constructible")
142	            skip += 1
143	        elif "com.code_intelligence.jazzer.api.FuzzerSecurityIssue" in out:
144	            # A Jazzer sanitizer fired (reflective call / SSRF / ReDoS ...). The method DID run on
145	            # both sides and did not diverge — this is a finding about the code, not a harness
146	            # failure, so it must not be lumped in with ERROR.
147	            sm = sorted(set(re.findall(r"FuzzerSecurityIssue(Critical|High|Medium|Low)", out)))
148	            tm = re.search(r"FuzzerSecurityIssue\w+:\s*\n(.+)", out)
149	            res, find = "FINDING", find + 1
150	            ev = f"Jazzer sanitizer ({'/'.join(sm) or '?'}): {tm.group(1).strip()[:40] if tm else 'see log'}"
151	        elif m and fe == 0 and "[DIFF-RAN]" not in out:
152	            # The harness "passed" without ever invoking both sides: every iteration bailed
153	            # because the arguments could not be built. Reporting that as EQUIVALENT would be a
154	            # false negative dressed up as a result, so it gets its own verdict.
155	            res, never = "NEVER-RAN", never + 1
156	            ev = "args never built in budget (no two-sided invocation)"
157	        elif m and fe == 0:
158	            res, ev, eq = "EQUIVALENT", f"no divergence in {dur}", eq + 1
159	        else:
160	            res, err = "ERROR", err + 1
161	            em = re.search(r"(NoSuchMethodException|NoClassDefFoundError|ClassNotFoundException|InstantiationException)", out)
162	            ev = (em.group(1) if em else "harness error") + " (skip)"
163	        print(f"{res}  (branch {branch})")
164	        with open(report, "a") as r:
165	            r.write(f"| {e['id']} | **{res}** | {runs} ({fe}) | {branch} | {line} | {ev} |\n")
166	
167	    with open(report, "a") as r:
168	        r.write(f"\n## Summary\n\n- EQUIVALENT **{eq}** · DIVERGENT **{div}** · FINDING **{find}**"
169	                f" · NEVER-RAN **{never}** · SKIP **{skip}** · ERROR **{err}**"
170	                f"  ({len(entries)} methods)\n")
171	        r.write(f"- Tested **{eq + div + find}** of {len(entries)} methods; the rest produced no "
172	                f"two-sided invocation. Only EQUIVALENT/DIVERGENT/FINDING are evidence.\n")
173	        r.write("- DIVERGENT = the two versions differ in exception type, return value, or receiver state after the call.\n")
174	        r.write("- FINDING = ran on both sides without diverging, but a Jazzer sanitizer fired on the code itself.\n")
175	        r.write("- NEVER-RAN = the harness completed but the receiver/arguments were never built, so nothing was compared. NOT equivalence.\n")
176	        r.write("- SKIP = structurally untestable (abstract receiver with no concrete subtype, unbuildable parameter type, pruned snapshot).\n")
177	        r.write("- ERROR = could not be tested (missing class at runtime, inaccessible member, bad manifest entry).\n")
178	    print(f"Done. EQUIVALENT={eq} DIVERGENT={div} FINDING={find} NEVER-RAN={never} "
179	          f"SKIP={skip} ERROR={err}  ->  {report}")
180	
181	
182	if __name__ == "__main__":
```

```text
27	/**
28	 * Reflection-based differential oracle, driven by a per-project JSON manifest.
29	 *
30	 * <p>A generated harness calls {@link #run(FuzzedDataProvider, String, String)} with its project
31	 * and method id. This engine looks the spec up in {@code /<project>/manifest.json}, resolves the
32	 * compiled {@code <Class>Original} and {@code <Class>Refactored} snapshots, builds the same
33	 * receiver and arguments for both, invokes each on a watchdog thread, and asserts equivalence.
34	 *
35	 * <h2>Identical inputs without deep-copying</h2>
36	 * Arguments are no longer restricted to scalars, so they cannot be cloned generically — and handing
37	 * both sides the same mutable instance would let the first call mutate it and make the second see a
38	 * different input. Instead this captures the iteration's fuzz bytes once and replays them into two
39	 * independent builds ({@link ReplayProvider}), giving structurally identical arguments that share
40	 * no references. Object construction itself is delegated to {@link ObjectFactory}, which uses
41	 * Jazzer's autofuzz and falls back to a concrete-subtype scan for abstract receivers.
42	 *
43	 * <h2>Equivalence</h2>
44	 * DIVERGENT iff the two sides differ in exception <em>type</em>, in return value, or in receiver
45	 * state after the call. Return values and receivers are compared by {@link Digest}, a structural
46	 * field walk, because domain classes inherit identity {@code equals()} and would otherwise diverge
47	 * on every input. A one-sided watchdog TIMEOUT is inconclusive, never divergent.
48	 *
49	 * <h2>Honesty about methods that never ran</h2>
50	 * A method whose receiver or arguments could not be built in any iteration would otherwise be
51	 * indistinguishable from one that ran clean, since neither reports a failure. The first successful
52	 * two-sided invocation therefore prints {@code [DIFF-RAN]}; a log without it means "never
53	 * exercised", not "equivalent".
54	 */
55	public final class GenericDifferential
56	{
57	  private GenericDifferential() {}
58	
59	  private static final long CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = Long.getLong("fuzz.callTimeoutMs", 3000L);
60	
61	  private static volatile boolean announcedRan = false;
62	
63	  private static void announceRan()
64	  {
65	    if (!announcedRan) {
66	      announcedRan = true;
67	      System.out.println("[DIFF-RAN] both sides invoked at least once");
68	    }
69	  }
70	
71	  // ── entry point used by the generated harnesses ─────────────────────────────
72	
73	  public static void run(FuzzedDataProvider data, String project, String id) throws Throwable
74	  {
75	    Spec s = spec(project, id);
76	    Class<?> oCls = Class.forName(s.original);
77	    Class<?> rCls = Class.forName(s.refactored);

79	    // One capture per iteration, replayed twice below.
80	    //
81	    // Deliberately NOT gated on a minimum length. An early version required >= 24 bytes so that
82	    // autofuzz had something to work with, which quietly destroyed the search: libFuzzer grows
83	    // inputs from a few bytes, and an input rejected before execution yields no coverage feedback,
84	    // so it never learns to grow them. A scalar target that needed 3 bytes before then found
85	    // nothing at all — a known divergence (WebServicesVersionConversion.getConverter) went

100	    // Permanent structural checks first, so an impossible target fails fast with a clear reason
101	    // instead of burning the whole budget returning from every iteration.
102	    if (!s.isStatic) {

104	    }

156	  private static Side buildSide(byte[] seed, Class<?> cls, Method m, Spec s)
157	  {
158	    ReplayProvider p = new ReplayProvider(seed);

160	    if (!s.isStatic) {

210	    String method;
211	    int arity;
212	    /** Source-level parameter type names, used only to disambiguate same-arity overloads. */
213	    List<String> sourceParams = new ArrayList<>();
214	    boolean isStatic;
215	    boolean isCtor;
216	  }
217	
218	  private static synchronized Spec spec(String project, String id) throws Exception
219	  {
220	    Map<String, Spec> byId = CACHE.get(project);
221	    if (byId == null) {
222	      byId = new HashMap<>();
223	      String path = "/" + project + "/manifest.json";
224	      try (Reader r = new InputStreamReader(
225	          Objects.requireNonNull(GenericDifferential.class.getResourceAsStream(path),
226	              "manifest not found on classpath: " + path), "UTF-8")) {
227	        JsonObject root = JsonParser.parseReader(r).getAsJsonObject();
228	        JsonArray methods = root.getAsJsonArray("methods");
229	        for (int i = 0; i < methods.size(); i++) {
230	          JsonObject m = methods.get(i).getAsJsonObject();
231	          Spec sp = new Spec();
232	          sp.original = m.get("original").getAsString();
233	          sp.refactored = m.get("refactored").getAsString();
234	          sp.method = m.get("method").getAsString();
235	          sp.isStatic = m.get("static").getAsBoolean();
236	          sp.isCtor = m.has("ctor") && m.get("ctor").getAsBoolean();
237	          JsonArray ps = m.getAsJsonArray("params");
238	          for (int j = 0; j < ps.size(); j++) {
239	            sp.sourceParams.add(ps.get(j).getAsString());
240	          }
241	          // Parameter TYPES are not taken from the manifest. Source parsing cannot resolve a
242	          // simple name like `Configuration` to an FQN without replicating Java's import rules,
243	          // and getting it wrong is a silent NoSuchMethodException. Arity plus the compiled
244	          // class is enough, and reflection then gives the real types.
245	          sp.arity = m.has("arity") ? m.get("arity").getAsInt() : ps.size();
246	          byId.put(m.get("id").getAsString(), sp);
247	        }
248	      }
249	      CACHE.put(project, byId);
250	    }
251	    Spec s = byId.get(id);
252	    if (s == null) {
253	      throw new IllegalStateException("id not in manifest: " + project + "/" + id);
254	    }
255	    return s;
256	  }
257	
258	  // ── resolution by name + arity ──────────────────────────────────────────────
259	
260	  /**
261	   * Find the method by name and arity on the compiled snapshot, disambiguating same-arity
262	   * overloads with the source-level parameter names from the manifest.
263	   */
264	  private static Method resolve(Class<?> c, Spec s) throws NoSuchMethodException
265	  {
266	    List<Method> exact = new ArrayList<>();
267	    for (Class<?> k = c; k != null; k = k.getSuperclass()) {
268	      for (Method m : k.getDeclaredMethods()) {
269	        if (m.getName().equals(s.method) && m.getParameterCount() == s.arity
270	            && !m.isSynthetic() && !exact.contains(m)) {
271	          exact.add(m);
272	        }
273	      }
274	    }
275	    if (exact.isEmpty()) {
276	      throw new NoSuchMethodException(c.getName() + "." + s.method + "/" + s.arity);
277	    }
278	    if (exact.size() == 1) {
279	      return exact.get(0);
280	    }
281	    Method best = null;
282	    int bestScore = -1;
283	    for (Method m : exact) {
284	      int score = 0;
285	      Class<?>[] pts = m.getParameterTypes();
286	      for (int i = 0; i < pts.length && i < s.sourceParams.size(); i++) {
287	        if (matches(pts[i], s.sourceParams.get(i))) {
288	          score++;
289	        }
290	      }
291	      if (score > bestScore) {
292	        bestScore = score;
293	        best = m;
294	      }
295	    }
296	    return best;
297	  }

299	  /** Does a reflected type plausibly correspond to this source-level type name? */
300	  private static boolean matches(Class<?> t, String sourceName)
301	  {
302	    String n = sourceName;
303	    int lt = n.indexOf('<');
304	    if (lt >= 0) {
305	      n = n.substring(0, lt); // erase generics: List<String> -> List
306	    }
307	    n = n.substring(n.lastIndexOf('.') + 1).trim();
308	    String actual = t.getSimpleName();
309	    return actual.equals(n) || actual.equalsIgnoreCase(n);
310	  }

312	  // ── invocation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
313	
314	  private static final class Outcome
315	  {
316	    final Object value;
317	    final String exception;
318	    Outcome(Object v, String ex) { value = v; exception = ex; }
319	    boolean threw() { return exception != null; }
320	    @Override public String toString() { return threw() ? "throws " + exception : "returns " + render(value); }
321	  }
322	
323	  private static Outcome invoke(Method m, Object inst, Object[] args)
324	  {
325	    try {
326	      return new Outcome(m.invoke(inst, args), null);
327	    } catch (InvocationTargetException e) {
328	      Throwable c = e.getCause() != null ? e.getCause() : e;
329	      return new Outcome(null, c.getClass().getSimpleName());
330	    } catch (Throwable t) {
331	      return new Outcome(null, t.getClass().getSimpleName());
332	    }
333	  }
334	
335	  private static Outcome invokeTimed(Method m, Object inst, Object[] args)
336	  {
337	    return timed(() -> invoke(m, inst, args));
338	  }
339	
340	  /** Run on a watchdog thread so a runaway input becomes a TIMEOUT rather than a stall. */
341	  private static Outcome timed(Callable<Outcome> body)
342	  {
343	    FutureTask<Outcome> task = new FutureTask<>(body);
344	    Thread t = new Thread(task, "diff-invoke");
345	    t.setDaemon(true);
346	    t.start();
347	    try {
348	      return task.get(CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
349	    } catch (TimeoutException te) {
350	      t.interrupt();
351	      return new Outcome(null, "TIMEOUT");
352	    } catch (Throwable e) {
353	      Throwable c = e.getCause() != null ? e.getCause() : e;
354	      return new Outcome(null, c.getClass().getSimpleName());
355	    }
356	  }
357	
358	  // ── oracle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
359	
360	  /**
361	   * Returns null when the two outcomes are equivalent, else a short reason naming what differed.
362	   *
363	   * <p>Order matters: exception type, then return value, then receiver state. A one-sided TIMEOUT
364	   * short-circuits to equivalent because it is timing-dependent and would otherwise manufacture
365	   * false positives on slow inputs.
366	   */
367	  private static String divergence(Outcome o, Outcome r, Class<?> returnType,
368	      Object oRecv, Object rRecv, boolean receiversStartedEqual)
369	  {
370	    if ("TIMEOUT".equals(o.exception) || "TIMEOUT".equals(r.exception)) {
371	      return null; // inconclusive
372	    }
373	    if (!Objects.equals(o.exception, r.exception)) {
374	      return "exception type";
375	    }
376	    if (!o.threw() && returnType != void.class) {
377	      if (isDirectlyComparable(returnType)) {
378	        if (!deepEquals(o.value, r.value)) {
379	          return "return value";
380	        }
381	      } else {
382	        String d = Digest.diff(o.value, r.value);
383	        if (d != null) {
384	          return "return value: " + d;
385	        }
386	      }
387	    }
388	    // Side effects on the receiver, but only when the two receivers started out equivalent —
389	    // otherwise a construction difference would be misreported as a behavioural one.
390	    if (receiversStartedEqual) {
391	      String d = Digest.diff(oRecv, rRecv);
392	      if (d != null) {
393	        return "receiver state after call: " + d;
394	      }
395	    }
396	    return null;
397	  }
398	
399	  private static boolean isDirectlyComparable(Class<?> t)
400	  {
401	    return t.isPrimitive() || t == String.class || Number.class.isAssignableFrom(t)
402	        || t == Boolean.class || t == Character.class || t.isEnum()
403	        || (t.isArray() && t.getComponentType().isPrimitive());
404	  }
405	
406	  /**
407	   * Value comparison that cannot throw. A domain class's own {@code equals()} is arbitrary code
408	   * and may throw; letting that escape would turn a testable method into a harness ERROR. On
409	   * failure fall back to the structural digest, which is total.
410	   */
411	  private static boolean deepEquals(Object a, Object b)
412	  {
413	    if (a == null || b == null) {
414	      return a == b;
415	    }
416	    try {
417	      if (a.getClass().isArray() && b.getClass().isArray()) {
418	        return Objects.deepEquals(a, b);
419	      }
420	      return Objects.equals(a, b);
421	    } catch (Throwable t) {
422	      return Digest.of(a).equals(Digest.of(b));
423	    }
424	  }
425	
426	  // ── constructor differential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
427	
428	  /**
429	   * A changed constructor is a test unit in its own right: build identical arguments for both,
430	   * invoke each, and compare exception type plus the structural state of the objects produced.
431	   */
432	  private static void runCtor(byte[] seed, Spec s, Class<?> oCls, Class<?> rCls) throws Throwable
433	  {
434	    Constructor<?> oc = resolveCtor(oCls, s);
435	    Constructor<?> rc = resolveCtor(rCls, s);
436	    oc.setAccessible(true);
437	    rc.setAccessible(true);
438	    for (Class<?> pt : oc.getParameterTypes()) {
439	      if (!ObjectFactory.maybeBuildable(pt)) {
440	        skip(s, "constructor parameter has no buildable form: " + pt.getName());
441	      }
442	    }
443	    Object[] argsA;
444	    Object[] argsB;
445	    try {
446	      argsA = buildCtorArgs(seed, oc);
447	      argsB = buildCtorArgs(seed, rc);
448	    } catch (ObjectFactory.Unbuildable e) {
449	      return; // transient
450	    }
451	    Outcome o = timed(() -> newInstanceOutcome(oc, argsA));
452	    Outcome r = timed(() -> newInstanceOutcome(rc, argsB));
453	    announceRan();
454	
455	    String why = null;
456	    if ("TIMEOUT".equals(o.exception) || "TIMEOUT".equals(r.exception)) {
457	      why = null;
458	    } else if (!Objects.equals(o.exception, r.exception)) {
459	      why = "exception type";
460	    } else if (!o.threw()) {
461	      String d = Digest.diff(o.value, r.value);
462	      if (d != null) {
463	        why = "constructed state: " + d;
464	      }
465	    }
466	    if (why != null) {
467	      Assertions.fail(String.format(
468	          "[DIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH] %s.<init>/%d%n  reason    : %s%n  ctorArgs  : %s%n"
469	          + "  methodArgs: %s%n  original  : %s%n  refactored: %s",
470	          simple(s.original), s.arity, why, render(argsA), render(argsA), o, r));
471	    }
472	  }
473	
474	  private static Object[] buildCtorArgs(byte[] seed, Constructor<?> c)
475	  {
476	    ReplayProvider p = new ReplayProvider(seed);
477	    Class<?>[] pts = c.getParameterTypes();
478	    Object[] args = new Object[pts.length];
479	    for (int i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) {
480	      args[i] = ObjectFactory.build(p, pts[i]);
481	    }
482	    return args;
483	  }
484	
485	  private static Constructor<?> resolveCtor(Class<?> c, Spec s) throws NoSuchMethodException
486	  {
487	    List<Constructor<?>> cands = new ArrayList<>();
488	    for (Constructor<?> k : c.getDeclaredConstructors()) {
489	      if (k.getParameterCount() == s.arity && !k.isSynthetic()) {
490	        cands.add(k);
491	      }
492	    }
493	    if (cands.isEmpty()) {
494	      System.out.println("[SKIP] constructor not found " + c.getName() + "/" + s.arity);
495	      throw new NoSuchMethodException(c.getName() + ".<init>/" + s.arity);
496	    }
497	    if (cands.size() == 1) {
498	      return cands.get(0);
499	    }
500	    Constructor<?> best = null;
501	    int bestScore = -1;
502	    for (Constructor<?> k : cands) {
503	      int score = 0;
504	      Class<?>[] pts = k.getParameterTypes();
505	      for (int i = 0; i < pts.length && i < s.sourceParams.size(); i++) {
506	        if (matches(pts[i], s.sourceParams.get(i))) {
507	          score++;
508	        }
509	      }
510	      if (score > bestScore) {
511	        bestScore = score;
512	        best = k;
513	      }
514	    }
515	    return best;
516	  }
517	
518	  private static Outcome newInstanceOutcome(Constructor<?> c, Object[] args)
519	  {
520	    try {
521	      return new Outcome(c.newInstance(args), null);
522	    } catch (InvocationTargetException e) {
523	      Throwable cause = e.getCause() != null ? e.getCause() : e;
524	      return new Outcome(null, cause.getClass().getSimpleName());
525	    } catch (Throwable t) {
526	      return new Outcome(null, t.getClass().getSimpleName());
527	    }
528	  }

530	  // ── rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
531	
532	  private static String simple(String fqn)
533	  {
534	    return fqn.substring(fqn.lastIndexOf('.') + 1);
535	  }
536	
537	  private static String render(Object v)
538	  {
539	    if (v == null) {
540	      return "null";
541	    }
542	    if (v instanceof Object[]) {
543	      return renderArgs((Object[]) v);
544	    }
545	    if (v.getClass().isArray()) {
546	      return arrayToString(v);
547	    }
548	    try {
549	      String s = String.valueOf(v);
550	      return escape(s.length() > 120 ? s.substring(0, 120) + "..." : s);
551	    } catch (Throwable t) {
552	      return "<toString threw " + t.getClass().getSimpleName() + ">";
553	    }
554	  }
555	
556	  /**
557	   * Escape non-printable characters in a reproducing input.
558	   *
559	   * <p>Fuzzed strings are full of control bytes and NULs. Printed raw, terminals and log viewers
560	   * swallow them and the recorded {@code methodArgs} reads as empty — which makes the one artifact
561	   * needed to reproduce a divergence by hand useless.
562	   */
563	  private static String escape(String s)
564	  {
565	    StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(s.length());
566	    for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
567	      char c = s.charAt(i);
568	      if (c >= 0x20 && c < 0x7f) {
569	        sb.append(c);
570	      } else {
571	        sb.append(String.format("\\u%04x", (int) c));
572	      }
573	    }
574	    return sb.toString();
575	  }
576	
577	  private static String renderArgs(Object[] args)
578	  {
579	    StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("[");
580	    for (int i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
581	      if (i > 0) {
582	        sb.append(", ");
583	      }
584	      sb.append(render(args[i]));
585	    }
586	    return sb.append(']').toString();
587	  }
588	
589	  private static String arrayToString(Object a)
590	  {
591	    if (a instanceof byte[]) return Arrays.toString((byte[]) a);
592	    if (a instanceof int[]) return Arrays.toString((int[]) a);
593	    if (a instanceof long[]) return Arrays.toString((long[]) a);
594	    if (a instanceof short[]) return Arrays.toString((short[]) a);
595	    if (a instanceof char[]) return Arrays.toString((char[]) a);
596	    if (a instanceof boolean[]) return Arrays.toString((boolean[]) a);
597	    if (a instanceof float[]) return Arrays.toString((float[]) a);
598	    if (a instanceof double[]) return Arrays.toString((double[]) a);
599	    return Arrays.deepToString((Object[]) a);
600	  }
601	}
```

```text
7	/**

9	 *
10	 * <p>This exists to solve an aliasing problem that only appears once the engine builds real
11	 * objects instead of scalars. The oracle must invoke both the original and the refactored method
12	 * on the <em>same</em> input; with scalars that was just {@code copy(args)}, but an arbitrary
13	 * object graph cannot be deep-copied generically. If both sides were handed the same mutable
14	 * instance, the first call could mutate it and the second would then observe a different input,
15	 * reporting a divergence that the refactoring did not cause.
16	 *
17	 * <p>The fix is to build the arguments twice rather than copy them once: capture the fuzzer's
18	 * bytes for this iteration, then replay those identical bytes into two independent builds. Both
19	 * sides get structurally identical arguments that share no references.
20	 *
21	 * <p>Determinism is the only contract that matters here — the decoding does not need to match
22	 * Jazzer's own provider, because the bytes still come from Jazzer and coverage feedback still
23	 * drives the search. On exhaustion the provider returns zeros and empty values (Jazzer does the
24	 * same) so a short input degrades instead of throwing.
25	 *
26	 * <p>NOT thread-safe, and not meant to be: one instance backs one side of one iteration.
27	 */
28	final class ReplayProvider implements FuzzedDataProvider
29	{

218	  {

220	    StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(n);
221	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
222	      sb.append(consumeCharNoSurrogates());
223	    }

231	  }

234	  public String consumeAsciiString(int maxLength)
235	  {
236	    int n = lengthFor(maxLength);
237	    StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(n);
238	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
239	      sb.append((char) (next() & 0x7f));

246	  {

248	    StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(b.length);

255	  /**
256	   * Length for a variable-size consume: one byte picks a size in [0,maxLength], additionally
257	   * capped by what is actually left so a 3-byte input cannot ask for a 100-element array.
258	   */
259	  private int lengthFor(int maxLength)
260	  {
261	    if (maxLength <= 0 || remainingBytes() == 0) {
262	      return 0;
263	    }
264	    int cap = Math.min(maxLength, Math.max(1, remainingBytes()));
265	    return (int) clamp(next(), 0, cap);
266	  }
```

```text
126	   */

128	  {

130	        || Modifier.isAbstract(t.getModifiers())) {

132	    }

134	    java.util.Arrays.sort(ctors,

136	    for (java.lang.reflect.Constructor<?> c : ctors) {

139	      }

202	  /**

208	   * loses to the plainest one, which in practice picks the project's straightforward
209	   * implementation over test doubles and inner adapters.
210	   */
211	  static Class<?> concreteSubtypeOf(Class<?> t)
212	  {
213	    Class<?> cached = SUBTYPE.get(t);
214	    if (cached != null) {
215	      return cached == NONE ? null : cached;
216	    }
217	    Class<?> found = null;
218	    List<String> names = classpathClassNames();
219	    List<String> ordered = new ArrayList<>(names);
220	    Collections.sort(ordered, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a.length(), b.length()));
221	    for (String name : ordered) {
222	      Class<?> c = loadQuietly(name);
223	      if (c == null || c == t || c.isInterface() || Modifier.isAbstract(c.getModifiers())
224	          || !t.isAssignableFrom(c) || c.isAnonymousClass() || c.isLocalClass()) {
225	        continue;
226	      }
227	      // A non-static inner class needs its enclosing instance; not worth the extra machinery.
228	      if (c.getEnclosingClass() != null && !Modifier.isStatic(c.getModifiers())) {
229	        continue;
230	      }
231	      if (c.getDeclaredConstructors().length == 0) {
232	        continue;
233	      }
234	      found = c;
235	      break;
236	    }
237	    SUBTYPE.put(t, found == null ? NONE : found);
238	    return found;
239	  }
240	
241	  private static Class<?> loadQuietly(String name)
242	  {
243	    try {
244	      // initialize=false: loading a random project class must not run its static initializer,
245	      // which can touch config files, spawn threads, or throw.
246	      return Class.forName(name, false, ObjectFactory.class.getClassLoader());
247	    } catch (Throwable e) {
248	      return null;
249	    }
250	  }
251	
252	  /**
253	   * Class names on the test classpath, restricted to the entries that can plausibly hold the
254	   * project's own classes: the compiled snapshots under target/test-classes and the project's own
255	   * jars. Scanning every dependency jar (Hadoop, Guava, Kryo ...) would cost seconds and only add
256	   * library types that autofuzz already handles.
257	   */
258	  private static List<String> classpathClassNames()
259	  {
260	    List<String> cached = classpathNames;
261	    if (cached != null) {
262	      return cached;
263	    }
264	    List<String> out = new ArrayList<>();
265	    String cp = System.getProperty("java.class.path", "");
266	    for (String entry : cp.split(java.io.File.pathSeparator)) {
267	      if (entry.isEmpty()) {
268	        continue;
269	      }
270	      File f = new File(entry);
271	      if (f.isDirectory()) {
272	        collectDir(f, "", out);
273	      } else if (entry.endsWith(".jar") && isProjectJar(entry)) {
274	        collectJar(f, out);
275	      }
276	    }
277	    classpathNames = out;
278	    return out;
279	  }
280	
281	  /** Heuristic: the locally installed project artifacts, not third-party libraries. */
282	  private static boolean isProjectJar(String path)
283	  {
284	    String p = path.replace('\\', '/');
285	    return p.contains("/org/apache/apex/local/") || p.contains("/local/")
286	        || p.contains("-local") || p.contains("-all");
287	  }
288	
289	  private static void collectDir(File dir, String prefix, List<String> out)
290	  {
291	    File[] kids = dir.listFiles();
292	    if (kids == null) {
293	      return;
294	    }
295	    for (File k : kids) {
296	      if (k.isDirectory()) {
297	        collectDir(k, prefix + k.getName() + ".", out);
298	      } else if (k.getName().endsWith(".class") && k.getName().indexOf('$') < 0) {
299	        out.add(prefix + k.getName().substring(0, k.getName().length() - 6));
300	      }
301	    }
302	  }
303	
304	  private static void collectJar(File jar, List<String> out)
305	  {
306	    JarFile jf = null;
307	    try {
308	      jf = new JarFile(jar);
309	      java.util.Enumeration<JarEntry> en = jf.entries();
310	      while (en.hasMoreElements()) {
311	        String n = en.nextElement().getName();
312	        if (n.endsWith(".class") && n.indexOf('$') < 0) {
313	          out.add(n.substring(0, n.length() - 6).replace('/', '.'));
314	        }
315	      }
316	    } catch (IOException e) {
317	      // an unreadable jar just contributes nothing
318	    } finally {
319	      if (jf != null) {
320	        try {
321	          jf.close();
322	        } catch (IOException ignored) {
323	          // nothing useful to do
324	        }
325	      }
326	    }
327	  }

329	  /** Scalar construction, split out so both this class and the ctor path share one definition. */
330	  static final class Scalars
331	  {
332	    private Scalars() {}
333	
334	    static boolean isScalar(Class<?> t)
335	    {
336	      return t.isPrimitive() || t == String.class || t == Integer.class || t == Long.class
337	          || t == Short.class || t == Byte.class || t == Character.class || t == Boolean.class
338	          || t == Float.class || t == Double.class;
339	    }
340	
341	    static Object build(FuzzedDataProvider d, Class<?> t)
342	    {
343	      if (t == int.class || t == Integer.class) return d.consumeInt();
344	      if (t == long.class || t == Long.class) return d.consumeLong();
345	      if (t == short.class || t == Short.class) return d.consumeShort();
346	      if (t == byte.class || t == Byte.class) return d.consumeByte();
347	      if (t == char.class || t == Character.class) return d.consumeChar();
348	      if (t == boolean.class || t == Boolean.class) return d.consumeBoolean();
349	      if (t == float.class || t == Float.class) return d.consumeFloat();
350	      if (t == double.class || t == Double.class) return d.consumeDouble();
351	      if (t == String.class) return d.consumeAsciiString(64);
352	      throw new Unbuildable("not a scalar: " + t.getName());
353	    }
354	
355	    static Object buildArray(FuzzedDataProvider d, Class<?> comp, int n)
356	    {
357	      if (comp == byte.class) return d.consumeBytes(n);
358	      if (comp == int.class) return d.consumeInts(n);
359	      if (comp == long.class) return d.consumeLongs(n);
360	      if (comp == short.class) return d.consumeShorts(n);
361	      if (comp == boolean.class) return d.consumeBooleans(n);
362	      Object arr = java.lang.reflect.Array.newInstance(comp, n);
363	      for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
364	        java.lang.reflect.Array.set(arr, i, build(d, comp));
365	      }
366	      return arr;
367	    }
368	  }
```

```text
=== demo original Widget ===
package example;

// A class whose constructor is UNCHANGED, so its methods get a working receiver and are
// judged on their own merits — one truly-equivalent refactoring and one genuine divergence.
public class Widget {
    private final int base;

    public Widget(int base) {
        this.base = base;
    }

    // Body changed but semantically equivalent (integer add is commutative/associative,
    // overflow wraps identically) -> EQUIVALENT.
    public int combine(int a, int b) {
        return a + b + base;
    }

    // Boxed-Integer param (exercises B1). Divergent vs the refactored version on negative
    // odd inputs: n / 2 truncates toward zero, n >> 1 floors -> DIVERGENT by return value.
    public int half(Integer n) {
        return n / 2;
    }
}

// Secondary top-level class, identical in both trees (exercises Fix C: it is relocated to
// its own Helper.java rather than duplicated into both snapshots).
class Helper {
    static int noop() {
        return 0;
    }
}

        return;
    }

        return;
    }
```

```java
package fuzz.auto;

import java.lang.reflect.Method;

/**
 * Dumps Jazzer's own coverage at JVM exit, in JaCoCo {@code .exec} format.
 *
 * <p>Jazzer already instruments every class it loads in order to drive its coverage-guided search,
 * so what it has accumulated by the end of a run is exactly "what the fuzzer reached" — a more
 * honest number than a second, independent JaCoCo agent, which also counts classes touched during
 * JUnit setup and manifest parsing. Jazzer exposes this as {@code --coverage_dump}, but that option
 * is only acted on by {@code FuzzTargetRunner.shutdown()}, which the JUnit integration never calls:
 * under {@code mvn test} the flag is silently inert (verified on 0.22.0 — passing
 * {@code -Djazzer.coverage_dump} produced no file). Registering the same two calls as a shutdown
 * hook produces the file the flag promises.
 *
 * <p>Everything here is reflective on purpose. {@code com.code_intelligence.jazzer.instrumentor} is
 * Jazzer's internal API, not its supported one, so a version bump may rename or relocate it. A
 * missing class must degrade to "no coverage file", never to a failed fuzz run.
 *
 * <p>Activated by {@code -Dfuzz.jazzerCoverage=<path.exec>}; {@code -Dfuzz.jazzerCoverageReport=
 * <path.txt>} additionally writes Jazzer's human-readable per-class summary.
 */
final class JazzerCoverage
{
  private JazzerCoverage() {}

  private static final String RECORDER = "com.code_intelligence.jazzer.instrumentor.CoverageRecorder";

  private static volatile boolean installed;

  /** Idempotent: the harness calls this on every iteration, but only the first one does work. */
  static synchronized void installIfRequested()
  {
    if (installed) {
      return;
    }
    installed = true;
    final String exec = System.getProperty("fuzz.jazzerCoverage");
    final String report = System.getProperty("fuzz.jazzerCoverageReport");
    if (exec == null && report == null) {
      return;
    }
    final Class<?> recorder;
    try {
      recorder = Class.forName(RECORDER);
    } catch (Throwable t) {
      System.out.println("[JAZZER-COV] unavailable: " + RECORDER + " not on the classpath");
      return;
    }
    Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(() -> dump(recorder, exec, report), "jazzer-cov-dump"));
  }

  /**
   * Flush the live coverage map into the recorder's covered-id set, then write the files.
   *
   * <p>The flush is not optional: Jazzer keeps the current run's hits in a native counter map and
   * only folds them into {@code additionalCoverage} when asked, so dumping without it yields a file
   * describing an empty run.
   */
  private static void dump(Class<?> recorder, String exec, String report)
  {
    try {
      Method update = recorder.getMethod("updateCoveredIdsWithCoverageMap");
      update.invoke(null);
    } catch (Throwable t) {
      System.out.println("[JAZZER-COV] could not flush coverage map: " + t);
      return;
    }
    if (exec != null) {
      invokeDump(recorder, "dumpJacocoCoverage", exec);
    }
    if (report != null) {
      invokeDump(recorder, "dumpCoverageReport", report);
    }
  }

  private static void invokeDump(Class<?> recorder, String name, String path)
  {
    try {
      Method m = recorder.getMethod(name, String.class);
      m.invoke(null, path);
      System.out.println("[JAZZER-COV] " + name + " -> " + path);
    } catch (Throwable t) {
      System.out.println("[JAZZER-COV] " + name + " failed: " + t);
    }
  }
}
```

```text
1	import java.io.File;
2	
3	import org.jacoco.core.analysis.Analyzer;
4	import org.jacoco.core.analysis.CoverageBuilder;
5	import org.jacoco.core.analysis.IClassCoverage;
6	import org.jacoco.core.analysis.ICounter;
7	import org.jacoco.core.analysis.IMethodCoverage;
8	import org.jacoco.core.tools.ExecFileLoader;
9	
10	/**
11	 * Per-method branch/line coverage from a jacoco.exec.
12	 * Usage: CovReport <jacoco.exec> <classesDir> [classSimpleNameFilter] [methodName]
13	 * Prints e.g.  DiskStorageRefactored.normalizeFileName branch=4/4 line=5/5
14	 */
15	public final class CovReport
16	{
17	  public static void main(String[] a) throws Exception
18	  {
19	    ExecFileLoader loader = new ExecFileLoader();
20	    loader.load(new File(a[0]));
21	    CoverageBuilder cb = new CoverageBuilder();
22	    new Analyzer(loader.getExecutionDataStore(), cb).analyzeAll(new File(a[1]));
23	    String classFilter = a.length > 2 ? a[2] : "";
24	    String methodFilter = a.length > 3 ? a[3] : "";
25	    for (IClassCoverage c : cb.getClasses()) {
26	      String simple = c.getName().substring(c.getName().lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
27	      if (!simple.contains(classFilter)) {
28	        continue;
29	      }
30	      for (IMethodCoverage m : c.getMethods()) {
31	        if (!methodFilter.isEmpty() && !m.getName().equals(methodFilter)) {
32	          continue;
33	        }
34	        ICounter br = m.getBranchCounter();
35	        ICounter ln = m.getLineCounter();
36	        System.out.println(simple + "." + m.getName()
37	            + " branch=" + br.getCoveredCount() + "/" + br.getTotalCount()
38	            + " line=" + ln.getCoveredCount() + "/" + ln.getTotalCount());
39	      }
40	    }
41	  }
42	}
43
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
3	# Install a target project's ALREADY-BUILT classes as local Maven jars, so the
4	# <Class>Original / <Class>Refactored snapshots resolve the rest of the project.
5	#
6	# This is the apex-core provisioning step (the -Papex-core profile depends on
7	# org.apache.apex.local:apex-*:3.7.0-local, which this produces). It is decoupled
8	# from any parent repo: point it at wherever you built apex-core.
9	#
10	#   Usage: scripts/setup_deps.sh <path-to-built-apex-core>
11	#          # <path> contains <module>/target/classes for: api common bufferserver engine
12	#          # e.g. a checkout built with `mvn install -DskipTests`
13	#
14	# Alternative: skip this and switch the four apex deps in the apex-core profile to
15	# Maven Central `org.apache.apex:apex-*:3.7.0`.
16	#
17	# Idempotent: re-running just re-installs. Safe.
18	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
19	set -euo pipefail
20	
21	BUILT="${1:-${APEX_CORE_HOME:-}}"
22	GID="org.apache.apex.local"
23	VER="3.7.0-local"
24	MODULES=(api common bufferserver engine)
25	
26	if [[ -z "$BUILT" ]]; then
27	  echo "usage: scripts/setup_deps.sh <path-to-built-apex-core>   (or set APEX_CORE_HOME)" >&2
28	  exit 2
29	fi
30	BUILT="$(cd "$BUILT" && pwd)"
31	
32	echo "Installing built apex-core modules as local Maven jars (${GID}:*:${VER})"
33	echo "  source tree: $BUILT"
34	echo
35	
36	for m in "${MODULES[@]}"; do
37	  classes="$BUILT/$m/target/classes"
38	  if [[ ! -d "$classes" ]]; then
39	    echo "  ✗ $m: $classes missing — build apex-core first (mvn install -DskipTests)" >&2
40	    exit 1
41	  fi
42	  n=$(find "$classes" -name '*.class' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
43	  jar="$(mktemp -d)/apex-local-$m-$VER.jar"
44	  ( cd "$classes" && jar cf "$jar" . )
45	  mvn -q install:install-file \
46	      -Dfile="$jar" \
47	      -DgroupId="$GID" -DartifactId="apex-$m" -Dversion="$VER" -Dpackaging=jar
48	  printf "  ✓ apex-%-12s %5s classes  -> %s:apex-%s:%s\n" "$m" "$n" "$GID" "$m" "$VER"
49	done
50
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provision EvoSuite, the automated unit-test generator that produces the seed
# corpus for the fuzzer (and a coverage baseline to compare the fuzzer against).
#
#   Usage: scripts/setup_evosuite.sh [<dir-with-existing-jars>]
#
# With no argument it downloads the official v1.2.0 release jars into tools/evosuite/.
# Given a directory, it copies the jars from there instead (offline / shared machine).
# Either way it also installs evosuite-standalone-runtime into the local Maven repo as
# org.evosuite.local:evosuite-standalone-runtime:1.2.0-local, which is what the generated
# *_ESTest_scaffolding.java needs on the classpath to compile and run.
#
# Version 1.2.0 is NOT on Maven Central (only the older 1.0.6 line is), so the jars come
# from the GitHub release. EvoSuite 1.2.0 also requires a Java 8 JVM to run — it reaches
# into JDK internals that are sealed from Java 9 on. The build itself is unaffected.
#
# Idempotent: existing jars are left alone unless --force is passed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -euo pipefail

VER="1.2.0"
BASE="https://github.com/EvoSuite/evosuite/releases/download/v${VER}"
MODULE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
DEST="$MODULE/tools/evosuite"
GID="org.evosuite.local"
LOCAL_VER="${VER}-local"

FORCE=0
SRC=""
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --force) FORCE=1 ;;
    *) SRC="$a" ;;
  esac
done

mkdir -p "$DEST"

fetch() {
  local name="$1" out="$DEST/$1"
  if [[ -s "$out" && $FORCE -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "  = $name (already present)"
    return
  fi
  if [[ -n "$SRC" ]]; then
    if [[ ! -s "$SRC/$name" ]]; then
      echo "  ✗ $name not found in $SRC" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    cp "$SRC/$name" "$out"
    echo "  ✓ $name (copied from $SRC)"
  else
    echo "  … downloading $name"
    curl -fsSL -o "$out" "$BASE/$name"
    echo "  ✓ $name ($(du -h "$out" | cut -f1))"
  fi
}

echo "Provisioning EvoSuite $VER into $DEST"
fetch "evosuite-${VER}.jar"
fetch "evosuite-standalone-runtime-${VER}.jar"

echo
echo "Installing the standalone runtime as ${GID}:evosuite-standalone-runtime:${LOCAL_VER}"
"$MODULE/mvnw" -q install:install-file \
    -Dfile="$DEST/evosuite-standalone-runtime-${VER}.jar" \
    -DgroupId="$GID" -DartifactId="evosuite-standalone-runtime" \
    -Dversion="$LOCAL_VER" -Dpackaging=jar
echo "  ✓ installed"

# EvoSuite 1.2.0 only runs on Java 8. Warn rather than fail: the generated tests compile
# and run on any JDK, so a mismatch only matters at generation time.
if ! java -version 2>&1 | grep -q '"1\.8'; then
  echo
  echo "  ! Default java is not 8 — EvoSuite $VER will likely fail to start."
  echo "    Point JAVA8_HOME at a JDK 8 (scripts/gen_unittests.py honours it), e.g.:"
  echo "      export JAVA8_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-openjdk-amd64"
fi

echo
echo "Done. Generate a seed suite with:"
echo "  python3 scripts/gen_unittests.py <project>"

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a unit-test suite for every method in a project's manifest, with EvoSuite.

    gen_unittests.py <project> [--budget 60] [--max N] [--force] [--side original]

EvoSuite is run once per *class* (not per method — it generates whole-class suites) over the
compiled <Class>Original snapshots in target/test-classes, i.e. exactly the classes the fuzzer
targets. The suites are the input to two later steps:

    scripts/unit_coverage.py   how much of each method the unit suite covers
    scripts/extract_seeds.py   the concrete argument values, which become the fuzzer's seed corpus

Why the ORIGINAL side: the differential oracle asks whether the refactored method still behaves
like the original, so the original is the reference the seeds should exercise. Pass
--side refactored to generate against the other snapshot instead.

Outputs, all under target/evosuite/<project>/:
    evosuite-tests/<pkg>/<Class>Original_ESTest.java             the suite
    evosuite-tests/<pkg>/<Class>Original_ESTest_scaffolding.java its runtime harness
    evosuite-report/statistics.csv                               EvoSuite's own coverage numbers
    generation.json                                              per-class status for later steps

Requires scripts/setup_evosuite.sh to have run, and a Java 8 JVM (set JAVA8_HOME if the default
java is newer — EvoSuite 1.2.0 uses JDK internals sealed off from Java 9 on).
"""
import argparse
import csv
import glob
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

MODULE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))

# EvoSuite's own default criterion set, minus the two that cost the most for what they add here.
# WEAKMUTATION drives assertion quality, which we do not use (seeds are argument values, and the
# coverage question is about reaching code, not about killing mutants); dropping it roughly halves
# generation time on the apex classes. CBRANCH/METHODNOEXCEPTION stay: they push the search toward
# distinct call outcomes, which is what makes a seed interesting to the fuzzer.
CRITERIA = "LINE:BRANCH:EXCEPTION:METHOD:METHODNOEXCEPTION:CBRANCH:OUTPUT"


def evosuite_jar():
    """Locate evosuite-1.2.0.jar: the provisioned copy, $EVOSUITE_HOME, or a sibling checkout."""
    candidates = [
        os.path.join(MODULE, "tools/evosuite"),
        os.environ.get("EVOSUITE_HOME", ""),
        os.path.join(os.path.dirname(MODULE), "RefAgent-reproduce/evosuite"),
    ]
    for d in candidates:
        if not d:
            continue
        hits = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "evosuite-[0-9]*.jar")))
        hits = [h for h in hits if "standalone" not in os.path.basename(h)]
        if hits:
            return hits[-1]
    sys.exit("EvoSuite jar not found. Run: scripts/setup_evosuite.sh")


def java8():
    """EvoSuite 1.2.0 needs a Java 8 JVM; the rest of the pipeline does not care."""
    home = os.environ.get("JAVA8_HOME")
    if home:
        return os.path.join(home, "bin/java")
    for d in ("/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-openjdk-amd64", "/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.8.0-openjdk-amd64"):
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "bin/java")):
            return os.path.join(d, "bin/java")
    return "java"  # fall back to whatever is on PATH and let EvoSuite complain


def project_classpath(project):
    """target/test-classes plus the project profile's dependencies, as one -projectCP string."""
    cache = os.path.join(MODULE, "target", f"cp-{project}.txt")
    if not os.path.isfile(cache):
        r = subprocess.run([os.path.join(MODULE, "mvnw"), f"-P{project}", "-q",
                            "dependency:build-classpath", f"-Dmdep.outputFile={cache}",
                            "-DincludeScope=test"], cwd=MODULE, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0 or not os.path.isfile(cache):
            sys.exit(f"could not resolve the {project} classpath:\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr}")
    deps = open(cache).read().strip()
    classes = os.path.join(MODULE, "target/test-classes")
    return f"{classes}{os.pathsep}{deps}" if deps else classes


def target_classes(project, side):
    """The distinct snapshot classes to generate for, in manifest order (deduplicated)."""
    man = json.load(open(os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/resources", project, "manifest.json")))
    out = []
    for e in man["methods"]:
        fqn = e[side]
        if fqn not in out:
            out.append(fqn)
    return out


def statistics(base):
    """EvoSuite's self-reported coverage per class, from its statistics.csv."""
    path = os.path.join(base, "evosuite-report", "statistics.csv")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return {}
    rows = {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            if row.get("TARGET_CLASS"):
                rows[row["TARGET_CLASS"]] = row
    return rows


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("project")
    ap.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=60, help="search seconds per class (default 60)")
    ap.add_argument("--max", type=int, default=0, help="only the first N classes (smoke test)")
    ap.add_argument("--side", default="original", choices=("original", "refactored"),
                    help="which snapshot to generate tests for (default original)")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="regenerate suites that already exist")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    jar = evosuite_jar()
    java = java8()
    cp = project_classpath(args.project)
    base = os.path.join(MODULE, "target/evosuite", args.project)
    os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)

    classes = target_classes(args.project, args.side)
    if args.max:
        classes = classes[:args.max]
    print(f"EvoSuite {os.path.basename(jar)} on {len(classes)} {args.side} classes "
          f"({args.budget}s each) -> {base}")

    results = []
    for i, fqn in enumerate(classes, 1):
        rel = fqn.replace(".", "/")
        suite = os.path.join(base, "evosuite-tests", rel + "_ESTest.java")
        if os.path.isfile(suite) and not args.force:
            print(f"  [{i}/{len(classes)}] {fqn} — reusing existing suite")
            results.append({"class": fqn, "status": "reused", "suite": suite})
            continue
        cmd = [
            java, "-jar", jar,
            "-class", fqn,
            "-projectCP", cp,
            "-base_dir", base,
            "-criterion", CRITERIA,
            f"-Dsearch_budget={args.budget}",
            "-Dstopping_condition=MAXTIME",
            # Keep the client in-process budget aligned with the search budget, or EvoSuite's
            # 120s global_timeout silently caps a longer --budget.
            f"-Dglobal_timeout={args.budget}",
            "-Dassertion_timeout=30",
            "-Dminimization_timeout=30",
            # Compiling and re-running the suite to check stability costs as much as the search
            # itself on these classes, and a flaky test is still a perfectly good seed source.
            "-Djunit_check=FALSE",
            # Deterministic runs, so a rerun reproduces the same seeds.
            "-Dstrategy=MOSUITE",
            "-Dshow_progress=false",
            "-Dwrite_covered_goals_file=false",
        ]
        t0 = time.time()
        log = os.path.join(base, rel.replace("/", ".") + ".log")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(log) or base, exist_ok=True)
        with open(log, "w") as lf:
            r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=MODULE, stdout=lf, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               timeout=max(300, args.budget * 6))
        took = time.time() - t0
        ok = os.path.isfile(suite)
        status = "generated" if ok else ("failed" if r.returncode else "no-suite")
        ntests = 0
        if ok:
            ntests = open(suite).read().count("@Test")
        print(f"  [{i}/{len(classes)}] {fqn} — {status} ({ntests} tests, {took:.0f}s)")
        results.append({"class": fqn, "status": status, "suite": suite if ok else None,
                        "tests": ntests, "seconds": round(took, 1), "log": log})

    stats = statistics(base)
    for r in results:
        row = stats.get(r["class"])
        if row:
            r["evosuite_coverage"] = {
                k: row[k] for k in ("Coverage", "BranchCoverage", "LineCoverage", "Total_Goals",
                                   "Covered_Goals") if k in row
            }

    out = os.path.join(base, "generation.json")
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"project": args.project, "side": args.side, "budget": args.budget,
                   "classes": results}, f, indent=2)

    made = sum(1 for r in results if r["status"] in ("generated", "reused"))
    tests = sum(r.get("tests", 0) for r in results)
    print(f"\n{made}/{len(classes)} suites, {tests} tests total  ->  {out}")
    return 0 if made else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Turn an EvoSuite suite into candidate fuzzer seeds: the concrete values each test case uses.

    extract_seeds.py <project> [--side original]

Reads target/evosuite/<project>/evosuite-tests/**/<Class>_ESTest.java and writes
target/evosuite/<project>/seed-values.json:

    {"<manifest id>": [{"test": "test0", "values": [{"type": "int", "value": -2816}, ...]}, ...]}

WHAT IS EXTRACTED, AND WHY THAT SHAPE
The consumer (fuzz.auto.SeedWriter) does not replay a test case; it re-runs the engine's own
argument-building code against a recording provider, feeding it these values in order. So what it
needs is not a resolved call tree but an *ordered pool of typed constants per test case* — the
values EvoSuite found interesting for that path, in the order they appear. SeedWriter tries several
ways of aligning that pool with the receiver and the parameters, and keeps only alignments that
verifiably decode back to the intended arguments, so a mis-association here costs a seed, never
correctness.

That is why this is a literal scanner rather than a Java parser. EvoSuite emits calls like
`Integer.getInteger("", 2419)` and `new Foo(bar0)` whose values only exist at runtime; resolving
them properly would mean interpreting Java, while their *literals* are exactly the constants worth
seeding. A test case is attributed to a manifest method when its body mentions that method's name.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys

MODULE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))

# Order matters: string/char before the numeric patterns, so a literal like "12" is not mined
# for the number inside it. Longs/floats/doubles before int, so the suffix is not left behind.
LITERAL = re.compile(
    r'"(?P<str>(?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"'
    r"|'(?P<char>(?:\\.|[^'\\]))'"
    r"|\b(?P<hex>0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+)[lL]?\b"
    r"|(?P<dbl>-?\b\d+\.\d+(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?)[dDfF]?\b"
    r"|(?P<lng>-?\b\d+)[lL]\b"
    r"|(?P<int>-?\b\d+)\b"
    r"|\b(?P<bool>true|false)\b"
    r"|\b(?P<null>null)\b"
)

TEST_START = re.compile(r"public\s+void\s+(test\d+)\s*\(")


def unescape(s):
    return (s.replace(r"\\", "\x00").replace(r"\"", '"').replace(r"\'", "'")
             .replace(r"\n", "\n").replace(r"\r", "\r").replace(r"\t", "\t")
             .replace("\x00", "\\"))


def literals(body):
    """Ordered typed constants in one test body, minus the JUnit noise."""
    # assertEquals/verifyException carry the *expected output*, not an input, and seeding on a
    # return value pollutes the pool with values no parameter can take.
    body = re.sub(r"\b(assert\w*|verifyException|fail)\s*\([^;]*;", "", body)
    out = []
    for m in LITERAL.finditer(body):
        if m.group("str") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "String", "value": unescape(m.group("str"))})
        elif m.group("char") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "char", "value": unescape(m.group("char"))})
        elif m.group("hex") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "long", "value": int(m.group("hex"), 16)})
        elif m.group("dbl") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "double", "value": float(m.group("dbl"))})
        elif m.group("lng") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "long", "value": int(m.group("lng"))})
        elif m.group("int") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "int", "value": int(m.group("int"))})
        elif m.group("bool") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "boolean", "value": m.group("bool") == "true"})
        elif m.group("null") is not None:
            out.append({"type": "null", "value": None})
    return out


def test_bodies(src):
    """Split a suite into (name, body) pairs by brace-matching each @Test method."""
    out = []
    for m in TEST_START.finditer(src):
        brace = src.find("{", m.end())
        if brace < 0:
            continue
        depth, i = 0, brace
        while i < len(src):
            if src[i] == "{":
                depth += 1
            elif src[i] == "}":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    break
            i += 1
        out.append((m.group(1), src[brace + 1:i]))
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("project")
    ap.add_argument("--side", default="original", choices=("original", "refactored"))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base = os.path.join(MODULE, "target/evosuite", args.project)
    man = json.load(open(os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/resources", args.project, "manifest.json")))

    # One suite per class; each manifest method looks for its own name inside that suite's tests.
    by_class = {}
    for e in man["methods"]:
        by_class.setdefault(e[args.side], []).append(e)

    seeds, stats = {}, {"suites": 0, "missing": 0, "methods": 0, "cases": 0}
    for fqn, entries in by_class.items():
        suite = os.path.join(base, "evosuite-tests", fqn.replace(".", "/") + "_ESTest.java")
        if not os.path.isfile(suite):
            stats["missing"] += 1
            continue
        stats["suites"] += 1
        src = open(suite, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        bodies = test_bodies(src)
        for e in entries:
            # A constructor entry is exercised by every test (they all have to build the object);
            # a named method only by the tests that call it.
            name = e["method"]
            cases = []
            for tname, body in bodies:
                if name != "<init>" and not re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(name) + r"\s*\(", body):
                    continue
                vals = literals(body)
                if vals:
                    cases.append({"test": tname, "values": vals})
            if cases:
                seeds[e["id"]] = cases
                stats["methods"] += 1
                stats["cases"] += len(cases)

    out = os.path.join(base, "seed-values.json")
    os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        json.dump(seeds, f, indent=1)
    print(f"{args.project}: {stats['suites']} suites ({stats['missing']} missing), "
          f"{stats['cases']} test cases -> {stats['methods']}/{len(man['methods'])} methods")
    print(f"  -> {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
