This is the part worth seeing, because it's where the two integrations meet. EvoSuite's generated tests call:

Those are the exact branch boundaries of `grade` — EvoSuite found them by search, and they arrive at Jazzer as input bytes. `Grader.grade` then hit **6/6 branches on both versions**, reported as "all 12 branches exercised".

**EQUIVALENT 3 · DIVERGENT 3 · SKIP 2** across 3 classes / 8 methods — identical to the pre-JavaParser run, so the parser swap changed nothing about the conclusions. 1,441,492 inputs and 129,369 differential comparisons in the 30s-per-method budget.

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run the whole differential-fuzzing pipeline from scratch, detached, in tmux.
#
#   scripts/run_tmux.sh [project] [duration] [unit-budget] [jobs] [--max N] [--fg]
#
#   project      pom profile id: apex-core (default) or example
#   duration     Jazzer budget per method          (default 30s)
#   unit-budget  EvoSuite search seconds per class (default 40)
#   jobs         EvoSuite classes in parallel      (default 10)
#   --max N      only the first N methods (smoke test)
#   --fg         run here instead of detaching into tmux
#
# FROM SCRATCH means the generated state is deleted first: the JavaParser tool and its AST
# output, the EvoSuite suites, the encoded seed corpus, the snapshots and harnesses, the
# carried-over libFuzzer corpus, and the previous report. Otherwise a run can pass on stale
# artifacts — EvoSuite reports "reused", the extractor never recompiles, and libFuzzer starts
# from inputs an earlier run discovered, so the report describes history rather than this run.
#
# apex-core is BIG: 27 classes, ~86 changed methods. Budget roughly
#   EvoSuite  ~= (27 / jobs) * (unit-budget + 20s)
#   fuzzing   ~= 86 * (duration + ~20s maven overhead)
# which is about 75-90 minutes at the defaults. Use --max 5 to smoke-test the wiring first.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -o pipefail

MODULE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$MODULE"

PROJECT="${1:-apex-core}"
DURATION="${2:-30s}"
UNIT_BUDGET="${3:-40}"
JOBS="${4:-10}"
MAXARG=""
FG=0
shift $(( $# < 4 ? $# : 4 )) 2>/dev/null || true
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --max) MAXARG="--max $2"; shift 2 ;;
    --fg)  FG=1; shift ;;
    *)     shift ;;
  esac
done

case "$PROJECT" in
  apex-core) ORIG="examples/apex-core/original"; REF="examples/apex-core/refactored" ;;
  example)   ORIG="examples/demo/original";      REF="examples/demo/refactored" ;;
  *) echo "unknown project '$PROJECT' — add its trees to this case block" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

SESSION="dfuzz-$PROJECT"
LOG="$MODULE/target/run-$PROJECT.log"

# ── relaunch into tmux unless we are already inside it ─────────────────────
if [[ $FG -eq 0 && -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
  if tmux has-session -t "$SESSION" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "session '$SESSION' already exists. Attach with:  tmux attach -t $SESSION"
    echo "Kill it first if you want a fresh run:            tmux kill-session -t $SESSION"
    exit 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "$MODULE/target"
  tmux new-session -d -s "$SESSION" \
    "bash '${BASH_SOURCE[0]}' '$PROJECT' '$DURATION' '$UNIT_BUDGET' '$JOBS' $MAXARG --fg 2>&1 | tee '$LOG'"
  echo "started tmux session '$SESSION'"
  echo "  attach : tmux attach -t $SESSION       (detach again with Ctrl-b d)"
  echo "  follow : tail -f $LOG"
  echo "  peek   : tmux capture-pane -p -t $SESSION -S -40"
  echo "  stop   : tmux kill-session -t $SESSION"
  exit 0
fi

# ── prerequisites, checked before anything is deleted ──────────────────────
fail() { echo "PREREQ FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[[ -f "$MODULE/tools/evosuite/evosuite-1.2.0.jar" ]] \
  || fail "EvoSuite missing — run scripts/setup_evosuite.sh"
java -version 2>&1 | grep -q '"1\.8' \
  || echo "  ! default java is not 8; EvoSuite 1.2.0 needs it (set JAVA8_HOME)" >&2
if [[ "$PROJECT" == "apex-core" ]]; then
  [[ -d "$HOME/.m2/repository/org/apache/apex/local" ]] \
    || fail "apex jars missing — run scripts/setup_deps.sh <path-to-built-apex-core>"
fi
[[ -d "$ORIG" && -d "$REF" ]] || fail "source trees not found: $ORIG / $REF"

echo "################ $PROJECT — FROM SCRATCH ################"
date
echo "duration=$DURATION  unit-budget=${UNIT_BUDGET}s  jobs=$JOBS  ${MAXARG:-(all methods)}"
echo

echo "---- clearing generated state ----"
rm -rf "target/parsetool" "target/ast-methods.json" \
       "target/evosuite/$PROJECT" "target/seeds/$PROJECT" \
       "src/test/Dataset/$PROJECT" "src/test/resources/$PROJECT" \
       "src/test/fuzzing/$PROJECT" "src/test/resources/fuzz" \
       "reports/$PROJECT" "target/fuzz-logs/$PROJECT" \
       "target/fuzz-cwd/.cifuzz-corpus" "target/cp-$PROJECT.txt"
echo "  parser tool + AST json, evosuite suites, seed corpus, snapshots, harnesses,"
echo "  libFuzzer corpus, previous report — all removed"
echo

START=$(date +%s)
python3 run.py "$PROJECT" \
  --original "$ORIG" --refactored "$REF" \
  --duration "$DURATION" --unit-budget "$UNIT_BUDGET" $MAXARG
RC=$?
ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))

echo
echo "---- optional: what the unit suite covers on its own ----"
python3 scripts/unit_coverage.py "$PROJECT" 2>&1 | tail -5 || true

echo
printf '################ ELAPSED %dm%02ds  exit=%d ################\n' \
  $((ELAPSED/60)) $((ELAPSED%60)) "$RC"
echo "report: reports/$PROJECT/auto-fuzz-report.md"
echo "RUN_COMPLETE project=$PROJECT rc=$RC"

```

Here's the script: [scripts/run_tmux.sh](scripts/run_tmux.sh)

```bash
scripts/run_tmux.sh [project] [duration] [unit-budget] [jobs] [--max N] [--fg]

scripts/run_tmux.sh                              # apex-core, 30s/method, all 86
scripts/run_tmux.sh apex-core 10s 20 10 --max 3  # smoke test (~5 min)
scripts/run_tmux.sh example 30s 30               # the demo instead
```

It self-launches into tmux — run it from a normal shell and it re-executes itself in a detached session, printing the attach/follow/stop commands. `--fg` runs it inline if you'd rather watch directly.

**It checks prerequisites before deleting anything** (EvoSuite jars, apex local jars, Java 8, source trees), so a missing `setup_deps.sh` fails with a clear message instead of wiping your state and then dying.

**"From scratch" means all of this goes first:** the JavaParser tool and its AST output, EvoSuite suites, the encoded seed corpus, snapshots, harnesses, the carried-over libFuzzer corpus, and the previous report. That last one matters — without clearing `.cifuzz-corpus`, libFuzzer starts from inputs an earlier run discovered and the report describes history rather than this run.

## Smoke test first (5m08s, exit 0)

I ran `--max 3` before committing to the long run, and the whole chain works on apex-core:

```
JavaParser  27 classes, 86 changed methods (7 ctor, 16 object, 63 scalar), 0 parse problems
prune       compile clean, 0 pruned
EvoSuite    24/27 suites, 337 tests
seeds       203 seeds for 45 methods, 590 rejected by verification
fuzz        EQUIVALENT 2 · DIVERGENT 0 · SKIP 1
unit cov    per-method branch/line reported
```

The 590 rejections are expected, not a fault: they're overwhelmingly methods whose object parameters the *engine* can't construct, so they were never seedable — the verification step is correctly refusing to write seeds that wouldn't decode to the intended arguments.

## Full run is now going

`dfuzz-apex-core`, all 86 methods at 30s each. Expect **~80–90 minutes**:

- EvoSuite ≈ (27 ÷ 10 jobs) × (40s + startup) ≈ 4 min
- fuzzing ≈ 86 × (30s + ~20s Maven overhead) ≈ 72 min
- unit coverage ≈ 5 min

Monitor with:

```bash
tail -f target/run-apex-core.log
tmux attach -t dfuzz-apex-core     # Ctrl-b d to detach
tmux kill-session -t dfuzz-apex-core
```

One thing to expect in the final numbers: this is the first full apex-core run since the JavaParser switch and the generic-aware object building, so it won't match the older 83-method figures. There are 3 more methods now (the ones the regex was swallowing), and the `object`-kind methods should reach further than before since collections are no longer built empty. I'll report the comparison when it finishes.
